name: Data Audit & Generator Forensics
purpose: Establish what the simulator actually produces before interpreting any downstream signal: schema, missingness, identifiers, split boundaries, class balance and known generator artifacts.
description: The audit resolves 1,852,394 transactions and audits 71 analytical columns. It fingerprints the two source CSVs, checks ten data contracts, establishes the temporal train/test boundary, and records the simulator behaviors that bound every later claim.
methods: ['Schema & completeness profiling', 'Data contracts', 'SHA-256 fingerprint', 'Identifier audit', 'Class balance', 'Temporal coverage', 'Generator forensics', 'Split integrity']
key_findings: ['Train and test are separated by a 48-second boundary, not a random split.', 'Eleven columns contain structural missingness from first-transaction history.', 'One data contract is flagged: minimum age is 13.9 years versus an expected ~18.']
limitations: ['Raw CSVs are not present in the workspace; only hashes and derived outputs are available.', 'The SHA-256 values were recorded as 16-character prefixes, not full digests.']

name: Univariate Distributions
purpose: Characterize the marginal distributions of amount, time, category, demographics and geography, and quantify how far fraud separates from genuine activity on each axis.
description: Twenty-four figures cover amount histograms, ECDFs, QQ plots, categorical rates, time profiles and demographic/geographic distributions. The phase establishes the first effect-size estimates rather than relying on p-values.
methods: ['Histograms & ECDFs', 'Box/violin & QQ plots', 'Quantile comparison', 'Category fraud rates', 'Temporal profiles', 'Demographic rates']
key_findings: ['Fraud amounts are shifted far to the right: median $390 versus $47.24 for genuine transactions.', 'The amount distribution is the strongest univariate separator in the program (KS D = 0.724).', 'Night hours carry a higher fraud rate than daytime volume would suggest.']
limitations: ['Univariate separation does not establish incremental predictive value.', 'Amount outliers are retained in the analysis; the maximum is 28,948.90.']

name: Bivariate & Interaction Analysis
purpose: Test whether risk concentrates in combinations of category, time, geography and cardholder behavior, and measure the money exposure behind transaction counts.
description: The interaction phase links category × hour, card profiles, city and ZIP3 structure, the fraud-dollar lens, mutual information and association structure. It distinguishes real structure from generator-driven artifacts.
methods: ['Interaction heatmaps', 'Cardholder profiles', 'Money-denominated rates', 'Mutual information', 'Spearman structure', "Cramér's V", 'ZIP3 EB shrinkage']
key_findings: ['shopping_net is the highest-volume high-risk category at 1.59% fraud versus a 0.52% baseline.', 'Merchant coordinates are jittered per transaction; distance is a simulator artifact, not physical travel.', '97.7% of cards experience at least one fraud event—an important simulator boundary, not a production prior.']
limitations: ['Merchant and category are almost redundant; merchant-level effects should not be over-interpreted.', "Geographic claims are restricted by the simulator's coordinate model."]

name: Temporal Structure
purpose: Determine whether fraud is temporally clustered and how volume, seasonality and structural breaks evolve across the 2019–2020 observation window.
description: Rolling statistics, weekly fraud-rate series, STL decomposition, ACF/PACF, time-profile heatmaps, PELT change-point sensitivity and card timelines are used to separate campaign-like clustering from calendar effects.
methods: ['7-day rolling statistics', 'STL decomposition', 'ACF / PACF', 'PELT change-point analysis', 'Time-profile heatmaps', 'Card timelines']
key_findings: ['Daily fraud rate has lag-1 autocorrelation of 0.503, evidence of temporal clustering.', 'Volume has strong weekly periodicity (lag-7 = 0.869); STL seasonality strength is 0.21.', 'Two consensus structural breaks are stable across PELT penalties; no holiday proximity was found.']
limitations: ['Two breaks are a small number of events; causal attribution to campaigns is not established.', 'The observations are simulated; calendar effects are properties of the generator.']

name: Advanced Visualization & Dimensionality Reduction
purpose: Test whether fraud separates without labels using embeddings, clustering and anomaly detection, and document the limits of visual separability.
description: PCA, t-SNE and UMAP embeddings are scored with logistic AUC. K-Means, DBSCAN and hierarchical clustering are profiled, alongside Isolation Forest, an autoencoder and LOF. High-dimensional visual encodings are evaluated for honesty.
key_findings: ['PCA(2) reaches logistic AUC 0.816; nonlinear embeddings do not improve separability.', 'Anomaly detectors isolate fraud only weakly (AUC 0.731–0.881).', 'DBSCAN labels 4% of points as noise, with a 6.08% fraud rate in that noise.']
limitations: ['Embedding AUC is a property of a 2D representation, not a deployable classifier.', 'LOF was evaluated on 5,000 rows versus 50,000 for the other anomaly models; AUCs are not directly comparable.']

name: Statistical Testing & Effect Sizes
purpose: Replace significance-only claims with effect sizes, bootstrap intervals, multiple-testing correction and inference that respects the card-level repeated measures.
description: Mann–Whitney tests are paired with Cliff's delta, KS statistics, bootstrap CIs and BH-FDR. Categorical associations use Cramér's V with post-hoc correction, and a card-clustered logistic model shows how naive standard errors mislead.
methods: ['Mann–Whitney U', "Cliff's delta + bootstrap CI", 'KS D + bootstrap CI', 'Benjamini–Hochberg FDR', "Chi-square / Cramér's V", 'Wilson intervals', 'Card-cluster-robust logistic regression']
key_findings: ["Fraud amounts show Cliff's delta 0.669 [0.656, 0.680] and KS D 0.724 [0.715, 0.732].", 'Five of eight logit effects survive card-clustered standard errors.', '72 of 91 category-pair post-hoc tests remain significant after Bonferroni correction.']
limitations: ["Cramér's V is not comparable across variables with very different cardinality (e.g., ZIP3 with 532 levels).", 'The logistic model uses a 200,000-row sample and 961 card clusters, not the full 1.85M rows.']

name: Feature Engineering & Depth Analyses
purpose: Build leak-aware behavioral features and test whether velocity, cohorts, hazards, hierarchical shrinkage and encoding choices add interpretable signal.
description: This phase constructs expanding, train-only target encodings, prior-transaction statistics and velocity features. It adds cohorts, discrete-time hazard, merchant hierarchical empirical Bayes, repeated-fraud events and an hour-encoding comparison.
methods: ['Expanding causal target encoding', 'Prior-transaction statistics', 'Velocity features', 'High-risk combinations', 'Cohort analysis', 'Kaplan–Meier + discrete hazard', 'Hierarchical empirical Bayes', 'Hour encoding comparison']
key_findings: ['Night + risky category + amount ≥ $500 reaches a 22.08% fraud rate, 42.4× baseline.', '38,005 transactions (2.05%) imply speeds above 1,000 km/h—physically impossible transitions.', 'No affected card has two distinct fraud events more than 7 days apart; compromises are bursty.', 'Fraud rate rises monotonically with implied speed and trailing-window counts.']
limitations: ['The high-risk combination is descriptive, not a causal effect.', 'The simulator gives fraud to nearly every card; cohorts and hazards are not production priors.']

name: Model Closure & Evaluation
purpose: Measure leak-free predictive performance, diagnose train→test transfer, calibrate probabilities and translate scores into review-budget economics.
description: A 27-feature LightGBM is evaluated with adversarial validation, per-feature PSI, walk-forward CV and leave-card-out CV. Calibration, cost-sensitive thresholds, capture@k, learning curves, ablation, SHAP, PDP/ICE and segment errors complete the loop.
methods: ['Adversarial validation', 'Population Stability Index', 'Walk-forward CV', 'LightGBM', 'Bootstrap PR-AUC CI', 'Calibration & temperature scaling', 'Cost-sensitive thresholds', 'Capture@k', 'Learning curve', 'Ablation', 'SHAP', 'PDP / ICE', 'Segment error analysis', 'Leave-card-out CV', 'Time-decay weighting', 'Monotonic constraints']
key_findings: ['Final model: test PR-AUC 0.5575 [0.5365, 0.5784], ROC-AUC 0.9677.', 'Walk-forward in-domain PR-AUC is 0.9510 ± 0.0152, but the same folds transfer at 0.4726 ± 0.0761.', 'Adversarial validation separates train and test at AUC 0.99999994; 7 of 27 features have severe PSI.', 'Top 1% of test by score captures 65.5% of fraud events and 68.7% of fraud dollars.', 'Removing card_prior_fraud raises test PR-AUC from 0.5575 to 0.8315, localizing the transfer failure.']
limitations: ['Test metrics measure out-of-distribution transfer, not typical generalization.', 'No epoch-level training history or hardware telemetry was logged.', "The final model's probability calibration is not directly comparable to the temperature-scaling split."]

name: Report & Reproducibility
purpose: Compile the graded findings ledger, figure/table index, reproducibility checklist and output bundle, and verify the expected phase-8 artifacts exist.
description: The closing phase writes 64 findings, 129 figure captions and an 11-item reproducibility checklist. It verifies 9/9 expected phase-8 tables and creates a 17.9 MB output bundle (not included in this workspace).
key_findings: ['64 findings compiled: 30 strong, 27 supports, 6 caveats and 1 weak.', 'All 11 reproducibility checklist items are marked true.', 'The notebook reports 9/9 expected phase-8 tables present.']
limitations: ['The 17.9 MB bundle referenced by the run is not present in the workspace.', 'The report summary says 45 tables, while 46 CSV tables are present.']
